expected_invariant: Every serial authority and transaction scenario owns a disjoint authored-synthetic UUID partition.
observed_error: AUTH-S01 derived its auxiliary user as actor+1, exactly overlapping AUTH-S02's primary actor; AUTH-S02 likewise used actor+1..4, overlapping AUTH-S03 through AUTH-S06. Attempt 001 stopped at the earliest overlap. The initial correction covered only the later AUTH-S02 overlaps, so attempt 002 reproduced the same earliest PostgreSQL unique-integrity failure.
detection_method: Attempts 001 and 002 both failed closed with hashed IntegrityError evidence after schema/catalogue admission and exact cleanup. A complete deterministic inventory then proved both derived-user families overlapped the primary actor partition and showed why the first partial correction could not affect the earliest collision.

correction.action: Move AUTH-S01 and AUTH-S02 auxiliary users into fixed high disjoint salt domains, prove their union disjoint from every scenario actor, and attribute any unexpected SQL error to its exact authority group before a final bounded runtime attempt.
correction.prevention_control: Behavior rehearsals with derived fixture identities must prove disjointness against every primary and subcase fixture index before runtime admission.
